title: Spiced lamb and swede with rice

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Lamb mince, swede, tinned tomatoes, rice, peas, yoghurt and ordinary spices are all things a grandparent would have kept.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded frying pan, a saucepan and a sieve, and the techniques are simple browning, simmering and boiling.

works.reason: 500g lamb, a small swede and 300g rice suit four, and 20 minutes covered with a tin of tomatoes and 200ml water will make 1cm swede tender without the pan running dry.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and dicing the swede and chopping the onion can be done while the lamb browns, so 25 minutes of active work and about 30 minutes of simmering are believable.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the mint, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming spiced lamb and swede braise suits early October, and the swede is a main part of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British instructions that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family dinner of meat, vegetables, peas, rice and yoghurt.
